title: C4CAM: A Compiler for CAM-based In-memory Accelerators
problem: CAM-based accelerator platforms currently require hand-crafted designs and low-level programming expertise, limiting accessibility to hardware experts. There is no automated compiler infrastructure to map high-level code to CAM platforms.
motivation: CAM-based systems efficiently support search operations critical to K-nearest neighbors, high-dimensional computing, and recommender systems, but current design barriers prevent their practical adoption.
method: C4CAM takes high-level Torch-Script code and converts it to hardware instructions step-by-step through multiple layers, where optimizations can happen. At each layer, the compiler automatically tries different ways to configure the CAM hardware and measures how each choice affects speed and power consumption, accounting for the differences in latency (response time) and power profiles across different CAM chip types.
key_novelty: The first compiler to automatically generate optimized code for CAM-based accelerators from high-level Torch-Script specifications.
contributions: First compiler framework for CAM-based in-memory accelerators
Hierarchical abstraction levels enabling progressive code lowering and optimized transformations
Automated exploration of CAM configurations and performance-energy trade-offs
Analysis of different CAM technologies' impact on system-level metrics
primary_theme: Compiler framework for CAM-based in-memory accelerators
